text:
### Observed differences

- The two central activities exchanged their participation and repetition. In the earlier window A05 appeared in every trace with about 4 occurrences per trace, while A10 appeared in about 47 of 100 traces with about 2 occurrences; in the later window A10 appeared in every trace with about 4 occurrences, while A05 appeared in about 50 of 100 traces with about 2. [OCC001, OCC003]
- Their typical positions in the trace exchanged accordingly: A05's mean position moved from about two-thirds to about one-third of the trace, A10's from about one-third to about two-thirds (event positions, not clock time). [POS001, POS003]
- Incoming routing flipped from A05 to A10: all observed outgoing transitions of A06 led to A05 before and to A10 after; A11 and A15, which had sent about half of their outgoing transitions to A05, now send about half to A10; A14's dominant target changed from A10 (about 51 in 100 transitions) to A05 (about 53 in 100). [DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR005]
- Outgoing routing swapped in parallel: A05 now leads to A17 in about 52 of 100 transitions where it previously led to A09, and A10 now leads to A09 in about 48 of 100 where it previously led to A17 (about 54 in 100). [DIR001, DIR003]
- The companion set re-anchored from A05 to A10: A09, A11, A14 and A15 each co-occurred with A05 in every earlier-window trace, and each co-occurs with A10 in every later-window trace while now appearing without A05 in about half of all traces. [REL003, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL020, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- Step distances moved with the rewiring: A14 is now followed by A05 typically within about 1 step (previously about 3), A14→A10 distances moved from about 1 step to about 3–5 steps, and A14→A16 from about 2 to 4 steps. [LAG005, LAG007, LAG008]
- Two further activities mirror the same shift: A08 fell from about 68 to about 34 of 100 traces (about 2.2 to about 1.1 occurrences per trace; mean position about 0.66 to 0.34), while A16 rose from about 30 to about 68 of 100 traces (about 0.9 to about 2.1 occurrences; mean position about 0.33 to 0.67). [OCC002, OCC004, POS002, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A05 and A10 exchanged roles: A10 took over the behaviour A05 previously showed — mandatory presence in every trace, about twice as many occurrences per trace, and a late position at about two-thirds of the trace, fed by A06, A11 and A15 and always accompanied by A09, A11, A14 and A15 — while A05 moved into the behaviour A10 previously showed, appearing in only about half the traces with fewer repetitions at about one-third of the trace, now fed by A14; the successor relations swapped accordingly (A05 now leads to A17 instead of A09, A10 leads to A09 instead of A17). [OCC001, OCC003, POS001, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL004, REL020, REL022, REL023, REL024]

The hypothesis is direct and consistent: participation, repetition and position reverse almost exactly between the two activities, and the successor changes, co-occurrence shifts and step-distance shifts all point the same way; with 55 qualifying items against roughly 0.5 expected if nothing had changed, chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole (each individual difference also exceeds those seen in about 199 of 200 random re-splits). [OCC001, OCC003, POS001, POS003, DIR002, REL020, LAG005, LAG007]

Limitations: all items derive from the same 2×200 traces, so they are not independent confirmations, and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows simply sample two different mixtures of existing variants — for example a different path becoming dominant — rather than a literal exchange of the two activities' roles; positions are relative event positions, so no clock-time rescheduling is implied. [OCC001, OCC003, POS001, POS003]

Other differences: A08 became rarer and earlier (about 68 → about 34 of 100 traces; mean position about 0.66 → 0.34) and now co-occurs with A09, A11, A14 and A15 in only about 34 of 100 traces (previously about 68), while A16 became more frequent and later (about 30 → about 68 of 100 traces; mean position about 0.33 → 0.67) and now co-occurs with A10 in about 68 of 100 traces (previously about 30) — the same up-and-late versus down-and-early pattern as A10 and A05. [OCC002, OCC004, POS002, POS004, REL013, REL016, REL025]
